idea: AI governance policy pack for small FCA-regulated firms
buyer: COOs and compliance officers at small FCA firms
pain: Staff use AI tools with no policy; compliance risk is unmanaged
v1: A template policy pack plus a two-hour workshop
channel: Her fund network and compliance consultants
verdict: Real compliance-driven urgency and genuine fit, but the purchase is one-off and low-priced.

why.distribution: 20-50 small regulated firms reachable directly, and compliance consultants would refer.
why.demand: Regulatory pressure creates genuine urgency, though nobody has been quoted yet.
why.fmf: She has run AI adoption inside a regulated firm - she knows what actually happens on the desk.
why.revenue_structure: One-off with a modest annual update; not a real recurring line.
why.defensibility: Compliance consultancies will bundle this within a year.
why.leverage: The pack is written once and sold repeatedly; the workshop is the only per-client time.
why.capital: Legal review of the templates: under £2k.
why.tailwind: Regulatory obligation with a real deadline is the strongest kind of tailwind.
why.ceiling: £4.5k x 30 firms = £135k, and 30 firms in year one is optimistic for a one-off product.

ceiling_arithmetic: £4.5k x 30 firms = £135k in year one, but the revenue does not repeat - year two starts from zero minus the £1k updates. Realistic: 12-15 firms = £55-70k.
carries: Compliance urgency, good leverage on a written product, and credibility from having done it inside a firm.
kills: Ceiling and repeat. A one-off policy pack is a project, not a business, and consultancies will absorb it.
test: Ask five compliance officers whether they have an AI policy and what they would pay for one.
test_pass: Two say they need one and name a budget.
test_fail: They say their existing compliance consultant is handling it.
